name: Obsidian Marrow

detectability.signature: Intense negative-mass energy signature surrounded by gravitational inversion shell; emits periodic bursts of exotic radiation across all frequencies

proximity: Gravitational sensors detect repulsive force gradients emanating from the anomaly's core
Standard matter brought near the boundary experiences molecular destabilization at the quantum level
Radiation shielding becomes progressively less effective as exotic particles interact with shielding materials
contact: Normal matter in contact with the exotic matter field undergoes rapid phase destabilization, losing molecular cohesion
Gravitational inversion causes catastrophic structural failure as load-bearing elements experience negative weight
Energy systems overload as exotic radiation induces uncontrolled energy release in conventional power cells
prolonged_exposure: Complete molecular dissolution of all standard matter within the exotic field
Exotic radiation exposure causes irreversible mutation at the cellular and genetic level in biological organisms
The exotic matter field gradually converts boundary-layer normal matter into additional exotic matter, slowly expanding its volume

behavior.cycle: Exotic radiation bursts occur at irregular intervals averaging 2.3 hours

phenomena: The core appears as a lens of absolute blackness with a glassy, vitreous surface texture that reflects no light yet somehow appears to have depth and structure
A halo of disintegrating normal matter surrounds the anomaly, glowing as it undergoes molecular dissolution in a ring of pale fire
During radiation bursts, the exotic matter core briefly becomes translucent, revealing internal structures that resemble crystalline bone or volcanic glass
Gravitational inversion near the boundary causes ejected debris to accelerate away from the anomaly at enormous velocities
hazards: The exotic matter field dissolves all conventional matter on contact, with no known shielding effective at the boundary
Exotic radiation bursts can damage vessels and crew at distances well beyond the visible anomaly
The anomaly's self-expanding property means its exclusion zone must be periodically updated
opportunities: Contained samples of exotic matter, if obtainable, would be among the most valuable substances in existence
The gravitational inversion effect could provide key insights into anti-gravity and negative-mass physics
Study of the conversion process could illuminate fundamental questions about matter-energy equivalence
known_incidents: The heavy cruiser Slab of Eternity attempted a close survey in 2508 using experimental exotic-matter shielding. The shielding failed at 340 kilometers from the core, and the vessel lost 40% of its hull before emergency thrust carried it to safety. Seventeen crew members died from exotic radiation exposure in the following weeks.
description: Obsidian Marrow is a compact elliptical concentration of exotic matter approximately 220 kilometers across at its widest, suspended in a halo of slowly disintegrating normal matter that gives it the appearance of a black bone exposed within glowing flesh. The core is impossibly dark, a vitreous blackness with the depth and texture of volcanic glass, yet it is not merely dark but actively repulsive to light, bending photons away from its surface in ways that give it an unsettling three-dimensional presence. During its irregular radiation bursts, the surface becomes briefly translucent, revealing internal crystalline structures of terrible beauty.

The anomaly's effects are extreme and begin well before the visible boundary. Gravitational inversion creates a repulsive field that accelerates loose matter away from the core at dangerous velocities, while exotic radiation penetrates conventional shielding with increasing effectiveness as distance decreases. At the boundary itself, normal matter simply ceases to cohere, its molecular bonds dissolved by interaction with the exotic matter field. Most disturbingly, the conversion process is not merely destructive but generative: dissolved normal matter becomes additional exotic matter, meaning the anomaly grows slowly with each interaction.

The origin and age of Obsidian Marrow are unknown, and both questions are subjects of intense and anxious debate. No natural process has been identified that can produce exotic matter in macroscopic quantities, yet the anomaly shows none of the structural regularity associated with artificial constructs. Some theorists have proposed that it is a fragment of a previous universe's physics, a relic where the rules of matter are simply different. Others, noting its self-expanding property, have raised the uncomfortable possibility that it is growing toward some critical threshold. The name was chosen for the anomaly's visual resemblance to exposed bone made of obsidian glass.

Obsidian Marrow carries the highest exclusion zone classification available, with a mandatory avoidance radius of 500 kilometers updated annually as the anomaly grows. Automated monitoring stations track its expansion rate, currently estimated at 0.04 kilometers per year, and model long-term projections. The scientific community is divided between those who advocate intensive study to understand and potentially contain the anomaly, and those who argue that any interaction risks accelerating the conversion process. In the meantime, the Marrow pulses silently in its halo of dissolving matter, growing imperceptibly, patient as stone.
